Coverage manifolds are modeled as differentiable manifolds parameterized by time and route-family inputs. The static assumption is a degenerate case where the manifold is constant. Scheme kernels define allowable transitions between manifolds, forming a dynamical system. Route families act as fiber bundles over these manifolds, constraining possible coverage configurations. In GSE, this manifests as state transitions governed by route-family alignment and coverage kernel validity. Failure modes include kernel collapse, where coverage schemas cannot adapt to new route families, and breakdowns in the topological structure when route complexity exceeds schema capacity. The dual nature of coverage—both static and dynamic—is resolved through the lens of manifold evolution under scheme constraints.
